people.name: Albert B. Fall

legalStatuses.matter: Conspiracy to defraud the United States with Doheny (indicted May 27, 1925)
Bribery: accepting $100,000 from Edward L. Doheny (Criminal Code § 117)

people.notes: Secretary of the Interior, March 5, 1921 – March 4, 1923. Over seventy at his 1929 trial (Fall v. United States), so necessarily deceased.

people.name: Edward L. Doheny

legalStatuses.matter: Conspiracy to defraud the United States with Fall (indicted May 27, 1925)
Bribery: giving $100,000 to Albert B. Fall

people.notes: Controlled Pan American Petroleum & Transport Co. and Pan American Petroleum Co. Public business figure of the 1920s; deceased.

people.name: Harry F. Sinclair

legalStatuses.matter: Conspiracy to defraud the United States — Teapot Dome lease (1928 retrial)
Contempt of the Senate — refusing to answer a Senate committee (R.S. § 102)
Criminal contempt of court — surveillance of the 1927 jury

people.notes: Organized and owned the Mammoth Oil Company (lessee of Teapot Dome). Deceased.

people.name: Edwin Denby
people.notes: Secretary of the Navy from March 5, 1921. Not charged in these sources. The Supreme Court found he was 'passive' but did know what he signed — do not portray him as deceived or as a conspirator.

people.name: Admiral John K. Robison
people.notes: Navy officer in charge of naval petroleum matters. The Court noted his motives for secrecy 'were not the same as Fall's.' Not charged.

people.name: Henry Mason Day

legalStatuses.matter: Criminal contempt of court — surveillance of the 1927 jury

people.notes: Sinclair's 'representative, friend and business associate' (his own sworn answer). Adult in 1927; deceased.

people.name: William J. Burns

legalStatuses.matter: Criminal contempt of court — surveillance of the 1927 jury (trial court)
Criminal contempt of court — surveillance of the 1927 jury

people.notes: Head of the William J. Burns International Detective Agency. His contempt conviction was REVERSED — he must never be described as convicted without the reversal.

people.name: W. Sherman Burns

legalStatuses.matter: Criminal contempt of court — surveillance of the 1927 jury

people.notes: Secretary and treasurer of the Burns detective agency in 1927. Deceased.

people.name: M. T. Everhart
people.notes: Fall's son-in-law; ranch manager. Never charged in these sources. Invoked the privilege against self-incrimination — not evidence of guilt. Prefer 'Fall's son-in-law' over his name in narration.

organizations.name: Continental Trading Company, Ltd.
organizations.notes: Canadian company; the record did not establish its owners.

organizations.name: William J. Burns International Detective Agency
U.S. Senate Committee on Public Lands and Surveys

Elk Hills (Naval Petroleum Reserve No. 1), California
locations.notes: Named 'Elk Hills' in the AP report; the opinions say Naval Petroleum Reserve No. 1.

locations.notes: Historical ranch of a deceased public official; town-level only.
